story.title: The Portrait's Alibi
story.logline: A convicted man realizes the oil painting of his crime scene is aging instead of him.
story.twist: The painting isn't aging to show his guilt; it is absorbing the years he was supposed to live in prison.
story.ending: How many decades does a masterpiece owe a innocent ghost?

scenes.narration: They locked me away for a murder I never committed, leaving my oil portrait in a dusty attic.
scenes.visual_prompt: Marcus, 35, short dark hair, wearing a gray prisoner jacket, standing in a dim concrete cell.
scenes.camera: Extreme close-up on eyes, fast push-in

scenes.narration: Ten long years crawled by in absolute darkness, but my face in the mirror refused to wrinkle.
scenes.visual_prompt: Marcus, 35, short dark hair, wearing a gray prisoner jacket, staring into a small steel mirror.

scenes.narration: Today, my parole officer brought me home and handed me the heavy, gold-framed canvas from the attic.
scenes.visual_prompt: Marcus, 35, short dark hair, wearing a gray prisoner jacket, holding a large oil painting.

scenes.narration: I wiped away a decade of dust, expecting to see the young man I used to be.
scenes.visual_prompt: Marcus, 35, short dark hair, wearing a gray prisoner jacket, wiping a dusty canvas with his sleeve.

scenes.narration: Instead, the painted eyes stared back at me sunken, bruised, and thoroughly ravaged by brutal time.
scenes.visual_prompt: Marcus, 35, short dark hair, looking at a portrait showing an old, battered man with gray hair.

scenes.narration: Deep wrinkles cut across the canvas forehead where my skin remains completely smooth and unblemished today.
scenes.visual_prompt: Marcus, 35, short dark hair, touching his own smooth face while staring at the old portrait.

scenes.narration: The frame grew heavy in my trembling hands as I realized the terrible truth of my sentence.
scenes.visual_prompt: Marcus, 35, short dark hair, wearing a gray prisoner jacket, struggling under the weight of the painting.

scenes.narration: The prison didn't hold my body inside those cold bars; it locked my physical decay inside this frame.
scenes.visual_prompt: Marcus, 35, short dark hair, backing away in terror from the aging portrait on the wall.

scenes.narration: I am entirely free to walk the streets now, yet I look younger than my own crime.
scenes.visual_prompt: Marcus, 35, short dark hair, standing in a sunlit room, looking healthy next to the decaying painting.

scenes.narration: If the canvas took every single year of my suffering, what happens when it finally runs out of paint?
scenes.visual_prompt: Marcus, 35, short dark hair, staring directly into the camera as the painting crumbles into dust.

caption.hook: The painting aged. He stayed young.
caption.title: The Portrait's Alibi
caption.caption:
Thirty years behind bars, yet his reflection hasn't aged a single day. The oil on canvas is bearing the sentence instead.

Are some prisons built inside our own frames?
